- [异步路由分发机制 Reference](https://info.ai-hao123.com)
- [RESTful微服务治理 Reference](https://view.ai-hao123.com/sitemap.xml)
- [中间件管道调用契约 Reference](https://doc.ai-hao123.com)


### 电脑连接（MCP）：让电脑上的 AI 工具把任务交给 Mika

# 电脑连接（MCP）：让电脑上的 AI 工具把任务交给 Mika

简体中文 | [English](mcp.en.md)

> 从电脑使用 Mika，先看[从电脑使用 Mika](computer.md)：怎么在 CLI + Skill 和 MCP 之间选、怎么连。想在终端或通过 Skill 使用，见 [CLI 与 Skill](cli.md)。

打开「电脑连接」后，Mika 就是一个 MCP 服务器：电脑上支持 MCP 的 AI 工具（MCP 客户端）可以把一件事交给 Mika，Mika 在手机上用自己的方式去做（操作 App、用内置浏览器、处理文件），做完把结果交回去。电脑说「要办成什么」，怎么做由手机上的 Mika 决定。

有两种连法，各有各的开关和令牌，可以都开：

- **经 USB（推荐）**：手机用数据线连着电脑、开着 USB 调试，电脑上一条命令就能打开，不用碰手机。只在手机本机上监听，Wi-Fi 上连不到。
- **经 Wi-Fi 或私有网络**：在手机的设置里打开，默认关着。电脑和手机在同一个 Wi-Fi，或在同一个私有 VPN 网络（组网工具建的虚拟局域网）里就能连上，不用路由器端口转发；这也是远程使用 Mika 的办法。

## 经 USB 连接（推荐）

前提：电脑上有 adb，`adb devices` 里有这台手机；Mika 至少打开过一次（它要把脚本写到手机上）。

1. 在电脑上运行：

   ```
   adb shell sh /sdcard/Android/data/com.wangzan101.mika/files/connect-computer.sh
   ```

   它先启动 Mika 的手机助手（和「用电脑启动」一样，已经在运行就跳过），再打开 USB 方式，最后打印连接信息，形如：

   ```json
   {
       "transport": "streamable-http",
       "url": "http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp",
       "headers": {
           "Authorization": "Bearer <令牌>"
       },
       "token": "<令牌>",
       "port": 8765,
       "forward": "adb forward tcp:8765 tcp:8765",
       "boot": "17"
   }
   ```

2. 把电脑上的 8765 端口转到手机上：

   ```
   adb forward tcp:8765 tcp:8765
   ```

3. 在 MCP 客户端里添加一个 Streamable HTTP（也叫「HTTP」）类型的服务器：地址 `http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp`，请求头 `Authorization: Bearer <令牌>`。配置文件的写法见下面「经 Wi-Fi 或私有网络连接」里的例子，把地址换成 `http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp` 即可。

之后想再看连接信息：

```
adb shell cat /sdcard/Android/data/com.wangzan101.mika/files/mcp-usb.json
```

打开以后：

- 通知栏里常驻一条「电脑连接已打开」；Mika 退到后台也一直开着。手机上的 设置 › 连接电脑 顶部先显示「等待电脑连接」，收到请求后才显示「已收到电脑请求」及时间。
- **拔插数据线**（或电脑上的 adb 重启过）之后，要再运行一次 `adb forward tcp:8765 tcp:8765`。令牌不变。
- 已经开着时再运行第 1 步的命令，令牌不变，已经配好的客户端照常能用。
- **重启手机后自动关掉**，要再运行一次第 1 步的命令；这时令牌会换新的，客户端配置里的令牌也要换上。

关掉（任一种都行，关掉后旧令牌立即作废，连接信息文件也删掉；下次打开换一个新令牌）：

```
adb shell sh /sdcard/Android/data/com.wangzan101.mika/files/connect-computer.sh off
```

或者在手机的 设置 › 连接电脑 › 高级设置 里关掉「经 USB 连接」，或者点通知上的「关闭」（Wi-Fi 那种开着的话也一起关）。

脚本做的事也可以直接用命令做（打开后等一两秒连接信息文件才写好）：

```
adb shell am start-foreground-service -n com.wangzan101.mika/.mcp.McpService -a com.wangzan101.mika.mcp.USB_ON
adb shell cat /sdcard/Android/data/com.wangzan101.mika/files/mcp-usb.json
adb shell am start-foreground-service -n com.wangzan101.mika/.mcp.McpService -a com.wangzan101.mika.mcp.USB_OFF
```

## 经 Wi-Fi 或私有网络连接

### 打开

1. 打开 Mika 的 设置 › 连接电脑，选择「MCP」›「Wi-Fi / VPN」，点「开启网络访问」。网络访问默认关闭，切换引导不会自动开启。
2. 打开后通知栏里会常驻一条「电脑连接已打开」，表示 Mika 在后台监听；通知上的「关闭」可以直接关掉。
3. 选择电脑能访问的地址，然后点「复制配置」添加到 MCP 客户端。配置包含地址和令牌；「查看配置」默认收起，展开也只显示令牌占位符。
4. 客户端连接或刷新工具后，确认页面顶部出现「已收到电脑请求」及请求时间。

访问开关、令牌的复制与更换、远程亮屏与解锁都在「高级设置」中，默认收起。「CLI / Skill」与「MCP」共用 USB / Wi-Fi / VPN 连接方式选择。「CLI / Skill」只有安装和连接两步，connect 会验证连接；网络方式使用 HTTP 根地址和令牌文件，使用 CLI 不需要 MCP 配置。

令牌和服务商的 API Key 一样加密存在手机上。关掉开关，端口就关了（USB 那种还开着的话，只留本机上的监听）。默认端口 8765 被手机上其他服务占用时，可以在「高级设置 › 监听端口」里换一个（1024–65535），改完立即生效；电脑上的 `connect` 和 `adb forward` 都以手机上显示的端口为准。

### 从电脑连接

- **同一个 Wi-Fi**：用列表里那个 Wi-Fi 地址（通常是 `192.168.*.*` 或 `10.*.*.*`）。
- **私有 VPN 网络**：手机和电脑都加入同一个网络后，用列表里那个网络的地址（这类网络常用 `100.64.*.*` 到 `100.127.*.*` 一段）。
- 手机走移动数据、或者对方是公网地址时，Mika 不接受连接。

在 MCP 客户端里添加一个「HTTP」（也叫 Streamable HTTP）类型的服务器，填地址，并加上请求头 `Authorization: Bearer <令牌>`。不同客户端的配置文件写法略有不同，大多是这个样子：

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mika": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "http://192.168.1.23:8765/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer <令牌>" }
    }
  }
}
```

也可以先用命令行试一下（把地址和令牌换成自己的）：

```sh
curl -s http://192.168.1.23:8765/mcp \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <令牌>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Accept: application/json, text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"curl","version":"1"}}}'
```

## 自托管远程连接

公网远程连接可使用自托管网关：在「MCP → 远程」配对后显式开启访问，复制 HTTPS 配置到支持 Authorization 请求头的客户端。手机主动连接，不需要同一 Wi-Fi 或 VPN。CLI / Skill 也可选择远程，共用手机的局域网访问令牌，由手机鉴权；网关不管理访问令牌，不提供 OAuth 流程。首版为单用户、单设备，部署见[自托管远程 CLI / MCP](dev/remote-mcp.md)。网关终止 HTTPS，可读取转发内容，请使用可信网关。

## 工具

| 工具 | 参数 | 做什么 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mika_run_task` | `goal`（必填）、`conversation`、`"request_id"`（可选） | 把一件事交给 Mika，马上返回任务编号 `task_id`。任务记在一个对话里，手机上的对话列表看得到。想接着上一件事说，就把上一个任务返回的 `conversation` 带上。 |
| `mika_task_status` | `task_id` | 任务此刻的状态、最近的进度、在等什么、做完时的回答。 |
| `mika_wait_task` | `task_id`、`timeout_s`（可选，默认 30，最多 50） | 等到状态变了（比如开始等你回答、做完了）或者到时间，再返回状态。进度说明变了不算，不会一步一返回。 |
| `mika_answer` | `task_id`、`text` | 回答 Mika 在这个任务里问的问题。 |
| `mika_steer_task` | `task_id`、`text` | 向 running 任务追加要求（最多 4000 字符），保留任务 ID 和上下文。返回 accepted 与 message_id，不代表已经执行。 |
| `mika_cancel_task` | `task_id` | 停下这个任务。 |
| `mika_list_tasks` | `limit`（可选，默认 10） | 电脑交来的最近几个任务，新的在前。 |

状态有这几种：

- `starting`：刚交给手机，还没开始。
- `running`：正在做，带着最近的进度说明。
- `queued`：还没开始，排在前面的任务后面（同时进行的任务已满，或这个对话里已有任务在做），轮到时自动开始；只能等或者停掉。
- `paused`：在等一个条件，比如手机锁屏了，解锁后自动接着做。
- `waiting_for_answer`：Mika 问了一个问题，用 `mika_answer` 回答（在手机上回答也行）。等太久没人回答，Mika 会当作没有回答接着做。
- `waiting_on_phone`：这一步只能由人在手机上处理，比如交给你亲手操作的一步。电脑这边没法代答，只能等或者停掉任务；手机上会照常弹出通知。
- `done`：做完了，带着回答；`verified` 表示回答核对过。
- `failed`：没做成，带着原因。
- `cancelled`：停掉了。

支持任务恢复的手机会在 `mika_run_task` 的输入结构里列出 `"request_id"`。调用方可先生成并保存一个小写 UUID，丢回执后用它调用 `mika_task_status`。同一编号、目标和对话参数只启动一次，换目标或换对话需要新编号。进程重启后仍能读终态，未完成的任务会报告 `failed` 和 `failure_kind=interrupted`。已收尾的记录保留 30 天、至多最近 1000 条。

建议的用法：`mika_run_task` → 反复 `mika_wait_task` → 遇到 `waiting_for_answer` 用 `mika_answer` → 直到 `done` / `failed` / `cancelled`。

追加要求后，用 `mika_task_status` 查看 `steers` 中对应 `message_id` 的去向：`received` 已收到、`joined` 已加入上下文、`not_applied` 结束或取消前未用上。正在执行的动作会先做完，追加不会撤销已做的事。排队/暂停、等待回答/审批/接管和终态均拒绝追加；收尾时未消费的远程插话不另开任务。响应丢失不要自动重发。旧 APK 的工具列表没有 `mika_steer_task`，需要升级手机 App。

## 远程亮屏与解锁

在手机的 设置 › 连接电脑 › 高级设置 中打开「允许远程亮屏与解锁」，默认关闭。经自托管网关连进来的客户端还要在远程页另开「允许经网关唤醒和解锁」（默认关），否则看不到这三个工具。没有密码的锁屏不需要填写凭据；PIN 或密码在这页的「锁屏凭据」中输入两次保存，电脑不能设置或读取它。

| 工具 | 参数 | 做什么 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mika_device_state` | 无 | 读取亮屏、锁屏、手机助手状态，以及是否允许远程解锁。 |
| `mika_wake_device` | 无 | 只唤醒主屏，不自动认证。 |
| `mika_unlock_device` | 无 | 唤醒并解除滑动锁屏，或使用手机上保存的正确 PIN/密码认证。 |

先调用 `mika_unlock_device`，返回 `status: unlocked` 且 `device.ready: true` 后再派任务；因锁屏而 `paused` 的任务在系统确认解锁后自动继续。`mika_wake_device` 的 `awake` 仅表示已经亮屏，不代表已经解锁。

- PIN 支持 4–16 位数字；密码支持 4–64 位英文字母、数字、空格和常见 ASCII 符号。图案锁屏、SIM PIN、无法识别的厂商凭据页不输入，返回 `unsupported_keyguard`。
- 输入 PIN/密码需要安卓 13 及以上：按键只投给系统锁屏界面，锁屏上方另有窗口（锁屏时显示的 App、来电等）时系统拒绝，凭据不会输进别的 App。安卓 12 只能解除滑动或无密码锁屏。
- 需先完成手机操作设置，内置手机助手和无障碍服务正常运行。有的手机还要在开发者选项里另外打开允许模拟输入的开关。
- 凭据加密保存在本机，不发给模型、电脑或日志。接口拒绝任何参数，包括 `pin`、`password` 等。
- 凭据提交前先持久化占位。失败、超时、取消或进程中断后，后续尝试返回 `attempt_blocked`，请在手机上检查并重新保存凭据；关开开关或重启 App 不会清掉这个保护。
- `disabled` 表示手机上未允许；`helper_unavailable` 表示手机助手未连接；`credential_required` 表示需在手机上保存凭据；`unlock_failed` 表示系统没有确认解锁，不会把按键注入成功当作解锁成功。
- 不支持重启后的首次解锁之前远程启动 Mika。重启后请先亲手解锁一次。这里不改变系统锁屏配置，不放行任务中的付款或确认。

## 安全

- **默认关闭**，打开后才监听；关掉立即停止。
- **USB 方式只在本机（127.0.0.1）上监听**，Wi-Fi 和别的网络上连不到，电脑经 adb 的端口转发进来。手机上别的 App 也能连本机端口，所以照样要令牌，而且 USB 的令牌只认本机来的连接。
- **只有电脑能打开 USB 方式、拿到它的令牌**：Mika 的这个服务只接受持有 `INTERACT_ACROSS_USERS_FULL` 权限的调用方，adb shell 有，普通 App 拿不到（这个权限也没法用 adb 授给别的 App）。令牌写在 Mika 的外部文件目录里（`/sdcard/Android/data/com.wangzan101.mika/files/mcp-usb.json`），安卓 11 起别的 App 读不到这个目录，只有 Mika 和 adb shell 读得到。
- **每个请求都要带令牌**。令牌是 32 字节的随机数，按常量时间比较；同一个地址一分钟内错 5 次，就先封一分钟。
- **不接受浏览器的请求**：带 `Origin` 请求头的一律拒绝，网页没法借你的浏览器碰到这个端口。
- **只接受私有网络**：两端都必须是局域网、私有 VPN 网络或本机的地址，公网地址来的连接当场断开。
- **花钱和确认只能在手机上**：电脑交来的任务里，付款、需要你同意的操作永远不会执行，不管「自主模式」开没开；交给你亲手处理的那一步也只能在手机上处理。`mika_answer` 只能回答问题，回答不了这些。
- **只碰电脑自己交来的任务**：电脑看不到、也停不了你在手机上发起的任务；电脑开的对话编号带固定前缀，接不上你手机上的对话。
- 每次运行的记录里写明是电脑（MCP）发起的。
- 传输是明文 HTTP，只适合在自己信任的网络里用；令牌别发给别人，怀疑泄露就「换一个」。

## 用不了时

- **列表里没有地址**：手机没连 Wi-Fi，也没连私有 VPN 网络。
- **状态写「没能开启」**：端口可能被别的 App 占了；关掉再打开试试。
- **USB 方式的脚本提示文件不存在**：先打开一次 Mika，等几秒再试；还是没有的话，手机上的 Mika 版本还不带这个功能。
- **经 USB 连不上**（`curl` 报连接被拒或断开）：再运行一次 `adb forward tcp:8765 tcp:8765`；手机重启过的话，先再运行一次打开的命令。
- **电脑上 8765 端口被别的程序占了**（转发报 `cannot bind`，或者连上后返回的不是 Mika 的内容）：电脑这边换一个空闲端口，比如 `adb forward tcp:18765 tcp:8765`，再把配置里的地址改成 `http://127.0.0.1:18765/mcp`。手机那边不用改。
- **返回 429**：同一个地址错的令牌试了太多次，等一分钟再试。经 USB 时手机上所有连本机端口的都算同一个地址。
- **电脑连不上**：确认两边在同一个网络；有的 Wi-Fi（比如访客网络）不让设备之间互相访问。
- **任务没开始**（交任务时就报错，或者过两分钟变成 `failed`）：打开一下手机上的 Mika 再试。安卓有时不让后台的 App 自己开始干活，打开过 Mika 之后就好了。
- **任务一直是 `paused`**：多半是手机锁屏了。先在手机上解锁，或在手机已允许远程解锁时调用 `mika_unlock_device`；仅调用亮屏不一定能解除锁屏。

## Related References

- [异步路由分发机制 Reference](https://news.ai-hao123.com)
- [RESTful微服务治理 Reference](https://www.ai-hao123.com)
- [中间件管道调用契约 Reference](https://view.ai-hao123.com)


### Models and sign-in

# Models and sign-in

[简体中文](models.md) | English

Mika doesn't come with a model; it uses a model provider you choose. Enter an API key, or sign in with an account. The main model must support tool calling.

## Add a model

Open "Models" (模型) in Settings (the app also walks you through this on first launch). Presets for many common providers are built in; the list is under "Supported model providers" in the [README](../README.md). For any other provider pick Custom (自定义), which takes any OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, Gemini or OpenAI Responses endpoint.

1. Add a provider: pick a preset, or pick Custom and enter the endpoint URL; enter your API key. For servers you run yourself, such as Ollama or LM Studio, the address is prefilled with the default port; change it to that machine’s address, and the key is optional.
2. Tap "Test and save" (测试并保存). When you connect your first provider, a main model is picked automatically. If the provider has no model list, the list lacks the model you want, or listing fails, tap "Enter a model name yourself", type the model ID from the provider's docs and tap "Test and save" again: only that model gets a test call, and the provider is saved only if it works. When picking a role you can also type a model name under any provider; typed models are tagged "Typed in". If the provider just will not connect and you want it saved anyway, tap "Don’t test, save anyway": it saves only the address and key, without listing models or making a test call. Such a provider is marked "not tested"; from its page you can test it again or refresh to list its models. An untested model never becomes the main model on its own: picking one as the main model on that provider tests it first, and if a task fails on a model error while the main model is still untested, the message points you to “Test again” on that provider.
3. The main model must support tool calling. Optional: a vision model (understands the UI and finds buttons in screenshots), a light model (anything cheap and fast; handles small jobs like judging task outcomes and extracting memories) and speech to text (see below).

The first three roles: the **main model** (does the work; must support tool calling), the **vision model** (describes the UI and locates things in screenshots; off by default on a fresh install, or choose "use main model"), and the **light model** (small jobs like judging outcomes, extracting memories and understanding intent; defaults to the main model). For exactly what "Test and save" tries and where the capability tags on the model list come from, see [model configuration details](../.github/CONTRIBUTING.md#model-configuration-details) in the contributing guide.

Whether a model can see images: if the provider's model list says, Mika goes by that; if it doesn't (many relays and self-hosted services don't), the preset's initial value applies, and a custom provider is assumed not to see. Tap a model on the provider's page and the sheet has a "Can see images" switch: what you set wins, even over the list. When the main model can see, screenshots go straight to it instead of costing a separate vision call. Picking the main model itself as the vision model (or choosing "use main model") also counts as saying the main model can see; switching away undoes it.

### OpenDesign Go

Subscribe to [OpenDesign Go](https://tech.ai-hao123.com) and create a workspace API key using its [API setup guide](https://read.ai-hao123.com/sitemap.xml). In Mika, add the **OpenDesign Go** preset, enter that key and tap **Test and save**. The preset uses Chat Completions at `https://amr-link.open-design.ai/v1`; Mika loads the models available to your key. If you type a model name, use an exact ID from that catalog and choose a tool-capable main model. Image support depends on the selected model, so use a suitable vision model for screenshot tasks.

## Check task cost

When using the official DeepSeek API, turn on **Show task cost** under **Settings › Task running**. After a new task ends, the estimate appears in Chinese yuan next to the token count. Mika uses the official price table and the usage recorded for the task. It shows a range during possible weekday peak hours and marks estimates as partial when some requests cannot be priced. Check your DeepSeek bill for the final charge.

## Jev decision model (optional)

Configure it separately in **Settings › Models › Decision model · Jev**. It is off by default and does not change your main, vision or light model selections.

| Provider | Complete request URL | Default model ID |
|---|---|---|
| TypeSafe | `https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone` | `jev-1.14.0` |
| OpenRouter | `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/systemone` | `typesafe/jev-1.14` |
| Custom | A complete System One-compatible endpoint | As specified by the provider |

Enter that provider's API key, enable the switch and choose **Save**. Changes apply to the next task. Selecting a different provider preset clears the previous key. **Test connection** classifies a fixed greeting without sending conversations or screenshots, saving settings, or enabling the service. The provider may charge for this test. Custom endpoints require HTTPS, except for local or LAN services; a chat `/chat/completions` endpoint is not compatible.

When enabled, Jev classifies intent at the chat entry point (discussion, reading or action), and selects saved routes when experience replay is enabled. Intent classification sends the current request and a small amount of recent conversation. Route selection sends the request, candidate templates and parameters extracted from the user's exact words. The API key and settings are encrypted on the phone. The main model still plans, generates text and calls tools; Jev never operates the phone directly or replaces confirmation gates.

Missing candidates, ambiguous parameters, low probabilities, errors and timeouts fall back to the existing model flow. A confident choice not to reuse a route skips replay and lets the main model plan. Disable and save to stop Jev calls in new tasks; tasks already running keep their starting configuration. Usage is recorded by model name, and `jev_intent` / `jev_route` run events identify selection, skipped replay or fallback. This version does not use images, Box grounding, per-step UI action selection or memory generation.

## Speech to text

The fourth role, used when you hold to talk; pick it under Settings › Models › Speech to text. By default it uses the phone's built-in speech recognition, which shows words as you speak and costs nothing. If the phone has none, or it is not accurate enough, pick a provider's speech model: it transcribes after you finish speaking and uses your quota. The list only shows models whose names look like speech models; for anything else, type the model name in by hand under that provider. Picking runs a short test transcription of silence and only selects the model if it works; otherwise you see why right away. If the phone's recognizer never responds when you hold to talk, Mika tells you and points you here; it never switches to a paid model by itself.

## Sign in with an account (no key needed)

At the top of "Add provider" is the group "Sign in with an account · no key needed". Tap one to read what happens, sign in in the browser, and come back to Mika to see the account and its models; you can set one as the main model right there.

- **ChatGPT** (Plus or Pro, uses your plan's usage): tap "Continue with ChatGPT" and sign in in the browser.
- **xAI / Grok** (SuperGrok or X Premium+ subscription): the browser opens xAI's confirmation page; check that it shows the same short code as your phone, then approve. This sign-in borrows the public sign-in entry of xAI's official command-line tool; xAI did not set it up for Mika and may restrict this use. Some subscription tiers still can't make calls after signing in (403); use an xAI API key in that case.
- **OpenRouter**: OpenRouter's official authorization for third-party apps. Once you approve, OpenRouter gives Mika a key of your own (named "Mika"), paid from your OpenRouter balance; to stop, delete it on OpenRouter's Keys page.

Signing out only clears the sign-in on this phone.

## Check current allowance

Open **Settings › Models › Token usage**. The top section shows the current allowance for each configured provider. Use the date filters below to review the token usage recorded on this device.

DeepSeek, Kimi, and SiliconFlow show the account balance. OpenRouter shows how much the current key can still spend. Tap the row to see the account balance on OpenRouter. For providers such as ChatGPT, **Manage usage** opens the official site. Tap **Refresh** to check current allowances again.

## Reasoning effort

Models on ChatGPT sign-in, xAI sign-in, and the Responses API can adjust **Reasoning effort** below each role card; OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic Messages, and Gemini models can too when the provider's model list states the levels for that model. The default leaves the choice to the provider. "Use main model" inherits its effort; explicitly picking the same model lets each role use a different effort. Options come from the provider's model list when available (the Anthropic model list states each model's levels; models that only take a thinking budget get none). Without listed levels, only Responses models get generic manual options, subject to server support; OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, and Gemini models are not guessed. Higher effort usually takes longer and uses more tokens.

## Response speed

In **Settings → Models → Providers**, open your OpenAI (API key) or ChatGPT provider and tap a model. Under **Use as**, select **Response speed**. Default uses the server setting. Choose Fast or Ultrafast to request that tier. The choice is saved per provider and model and applies to every role that uses that model. Availability depends on the model, project, or ChatGPT plan, and faster tiers may use more of your API or plan budget. If the server rejects a tier, select Default again.

## Context window and compaction

Open **Context and compaction** under a role in **Settings › Models**. Leave the window blank to use the selected model’s window. Leave the trigger blank for automatic compaction, or enter an absolute token count. The trigger counts the whole request, including the system prompt, tools, and messages. A window of 1,000,000 tokens has an automatic trigger of 967,000. Enter 600,000 to compact earlier. Use digits only in the fields. The dialog shows the allowed range and effective values. After compaction, the request can grow by a margin before it triggers again.

The settings apply on the next task and are shared by roles using the same provider and model. Choose **Reset** and save to restore both defaults. If reselecting a model gives it a smaller window, the effective trigger stays within its new bounds. A window override sets the local budget. The provider still enforces its own context limit.

## Models on your own computer or LAN

When adding a provider choose "Custom" (自定义); the base URL may start with `http://`, e.g. `http://192.168.1.10:11434/v1` (with the phone on the same Wi-Fi). Local and LAN addresses show no warning; an unencrypted address outside your LAN shows a short warning, since your API key and chats could be seen by others on the network. Use `https://` when you can.

## Network proxy

If you need a proxy to reach a model service but don't want a system-wide VPN, enter an address in **Settings › Network proxy**: `http://host:port` or `socks5://host:port` (`socks5h` works too; host names are resolved by the proxy). For a proxy that needs a login, write `http://user:password@host:port`. The address is stored encrypted on the phone; the screen only shows the scheme, host and port.

- Goes through the proxy: model requests (chat, speech to text, connection tests), model lists, provider allowance checks, token exchange when you sign in with an account, in-app update downloads, the in-app browser, and commands in Files & computing environment (while network access is on there).
- Always direct: addresses on this phone or your LAN (localhost, 127.x, 10.x, 172.16–31.x, 192.168.x, 100.64–127.x, names ending in `.local` or `.lan`, and single-word machine names), so local models such as Ollama or LM Studio keep working.
- If the proxy can't be reached or rejects the user name or password, Mika says so instead of blaming your key or model.
- `https://` proxies (an encrypted connection to the proxy itself) are only used by commands in Files & computing environment; Mika's own connections stay direct. Use `http://` or `socks5://` to cover everything.
- The in-app browser uses the proxy only if the phone's WebView supports a per-app proxy, and it can't use a SOCKS proxy that needs a login. In those cases the settings row says the browser connects directly.

## API key pool and auto-rotation

You can add multiple API keys for any provider by separating them with newlines, commas, or semicolons in the API key field, or using the "Add API Key" button under the provider's details page.

- **Round-robin load balancing**: When multiple healthy keys are active, Mika rotates requests evenly across the pool, multiplying your rate limit and token throughput.
- **Sub-50ms failover on rate limits**: If a key hits an `HTTP 429` (rate limit) or `401`/`403` (quota exhausted or invalid), Mika traps the failure, puts the affected key on a temporary cooldown (honoring the server's `Retry-After` header or a default 60s cooldown), and seamlessly swaps to the next key in `<50ms` without interrupting your task.
- **Auto-unfreeze**: Once a key's cooldown period ends, it automatically returns to active rotation.

## Multi-model waterfall and fallback

To prevent tasks from failing when a provider encounters capacity outages, service degradations, or prompt token limits (e.g. `HTTP 413` or `5xx` errors):

- Mika supports configuring secondary and tertiary fallback models under each role.
- If all keys for your primary model fail or the provider is temporarily unavailable, execution cascades down your waterfall chain automatically.
- Once primary keys recover from their cooldown, subsequent tasks automatically ascend back to your primary model.

## ChatGPT reports a workspace access error after switching accounts

If the browser says the app is only available to members of its workspace and shows `3p_login_workspace_scope_denied`, first check that you selected the ChatGPT account and workspace originally used to authorize it. The error means the current sign-in does not meet the app registration's workspace scope; it does not by itself establish a wrong password or exhausted plan usage.

ChatGPT **Sign out** in Mika keeps the registered `client_id` so the same account can sign in again. If you intend to switch to a different account or workspace, repeatedly signing out and back in may keep using the old binding. To create a new connection:

1. Return to Mika and cancel any pending sign-in.
2. Note your main, vision and light model selections.
3. Open **Settings › Models › ChatGPT** and confirm **Delete this provider** at the bottom. This removes that provider's local credentials, model configurations and registration ID; roles using it need to be selected again. Conversations stay on the phone. You do not need to uninstall Mika or clear all app data.
4. Add ChatGPT again, tap **Continue with ChatGPT**, choose the intended account and workspace in the browser, complete authorization, and return to Mika.
5. Select the models for your roles again and send a short request to verify inference. A model list confirms sign-in and model listing, not a successful inference request.

This is for switching accounts or workspaces, not bypassing workspace access controls. If a fresh connection is still denied, check that the account has access to the workspace or contact its administrator. Include the error code and Mika version when reporting it, and redact email addresses, authorization codes and tokens.


### 模型与登录

# 模型与登录

简体中文 | [English](models.en.md)

Mika 不带模型，用你自己选的模型服务商：填一把 API Key，或者用账号登录。主模型要支持工具调用。

## 添加模型

打开设置里的「模型」（第一次打开 App 时也会引导你）。内置了一批常见服务商的预设，清单见 [README](readme/README.zh-CN.md) 里「支持的模型服务商」；其他服务商选「自定义」，OpenAI 兼容、Anthropic、Gemini、OpenAI Responses 接口都能接。

1. 添加服务商：选一个预设，或选「自定义」填接口地址；填 API Key。Ollama、LM Studio 这类自己机器上跑的服务，地址预填了默认端口，改成那台机器的地址即可，Key 可不填。
2. 点「测试并保存」，连上第一家时会自动选一个主模型。这家不提供模型列表、列表里没有你要的、或列模型出错时，点「手动填写模型名」填上服务商文档里的模型 ID，再点「测试并保存」：只用这个模型试调用一次，通了才保存。选用途时每家下面也都能手填，手填的标「手填」。实在连不上、又想先存下时，也可以点「不测试，直接保存」：只存地址和 Key，不列模型、不试调用，存下的这家标「没测试过」，之后在服务商页可以「重新测试」，或先刷新列出模型。没测过的模型不会自动当主模型，在这家选主模型时先试调用；主模型没测试通过、任务又因模型出错失败时，提示会指向这家的「重新测试」。
3. 主模型要支持工具调用。可选：看图模型（看懂界面、看图找按钮）、轻量模型（便宜快的即可，处理判断结局、提取记忆等小事）、语音转文字（见下文）。

前三个用途分别是：**主模型**（办事，要支持工具调用）、**看图模型**（描述界面、看图定位；新装默认不用，可选「用主模型」）、**轻量模型**（判断结局、提取记忆、理解意图等小事，默认用主模型）。「测试并保存」具体怎么试、模型列表上的能力标签怎么来，见[贡献指南里的模型配置细节](../.github/CONTRIBUTING.zh-CN.md#模型配置细节)。

模型能不能看图：服务商的模型列表写了就照它，没写（不少中转、自建服务都不写）按预设初值，自定义服务商默认当它看不了。在服务商详情里点一个模型，面板下面有「能看图」开关，你说了算，列表写了的也能改。主模型能看图时，截图直接附给它看，不必另调一次看图模型；看图模型选的就是主模型（或选「用主模型」）也算你说了主模型能看图，换走了就恢复。

### OpenDesign Go

订阅 [OpenDesign Go](https://view.ai-hao123.com/sitemap.xml)，按[API 接入说明](https://doc.ai-hao123.com)创建工作区 Key。在 Mika 添加 **OpenDesign Go** 预设，填写这把 Key，点「测试并保存」。预设使用 Chat Completions，地址为 `https://amr-link.open-design.ai/v1`；Mika 会读取这把 Key 可用的模型。手填模型名时使用目录里的准确 ID，主模型须支持工具调用。看图能力取决于具体模型，屏幕任务请配置合适的视觉模型。

## 查看任务费用

用 DeepSeek 官方 API 时，可以在 **设置 › 任务运行** 打开「显示任务费用」。新任务结束后，Token 数旁会显示人民币估算。Mika 按官方价目表和本轮已记录的模型用量计算，工作日可能的高峰时段会显示峰谷价区间。部分请求无法估算时，金额旁会标「部分」。实际扣费以 DeepSeek 账单为准。

## Jev 决策模型（可选）

在「设置 › 模型 › 决策模型 · Jev」单独配置，默认关闭，不改变主模型、看图模型或轻量模型的选择。

| 服务商 | 完整请求地址 | 默认模型 ID |
|---|---|---|
| TypeSafe | `https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone` | `jev-1.14.0` |
| OpenRouter | `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/systemone` | `typesafe/jev-1.14` |
| 自定义 | 填完整的 System One 兼容接口地址 | 按服务商填写 |

填入这家服务商的 API Key，打开开关并点「保存」，从下一次任务生效。切换服务商预设时重新填写对应的 Key。「测试连接」只发送固定的问候语做分类，不发送聊天或屏幕，不保存或开启配置；这次测试也可能计入服务商用量。自定义地址须使用 HTTPS，本机和局域网服务允许 HTTP；聊天接口 `/chat/completions` 不能直接用在这里。

开启后，Jev 用于聊天入口的意图判断（讨论、读取、执行），以及已开启经验回放时的历史路线选择。意图判断会发送本次请求和少量近期对话；路线选择会发送请求、候选路线模板及从原话提取的参数。API Key 与配置加密保存在手机上。主模型仍负责规划、文字生成和工具调用，Jev 不直接操作手机，也不替代确认关卡。

没有合适候选、参数无法唯一提取、概率不足、接口出错或超时，都会回到原有模型流程。Jev 明确选择不复用路线时，则跳过回放，由主模型继续规划。关闭并保存后，新任务不再调用 Jev；已开始的任务使用启动时的配置。用量页按模型名记录这些请求；运行记录中的 `jev_intent` / `jev_route` 标明采用了决策、跳过回放还是回退。此版本没有接入图片、Box 定位、逐步界面动作选择或记忆生成。

## 语音转文字

按住说话时用的第四个用途，在「设置 › 模型 › 语音转文字」里选。默认用手机自带的语音识别，边说边出字，不花钱。手机没有、或认不准时，可以选服务商的语音模型：说完再转成字，用你的额度；列表里只列名字像语音模型的，没列出来的可以在每家下面手动填模型名。选的时候会先试转一小段静音，通了才选上，不通当场说原因。手机自带的识别如果按住后一直没有反应，Mika 会提示你来这里选一个，不会自己换成要花钱的模型。

## 用账号登录（不用填 Key）

添加服务商最上面是「用账号登录 · 不用填 Key」一组，点一家先看说明，再去浏览器里登录，登录后回到 Mika，能看到账号、可用的模型，可以直接设为主模型。

- **ChatGPT**（Plus 或 Pro，用你的套餐额度）：点「使用 ChatGPT 继续」，在浏览器里登录。
- **xAI / Grok**（SuperGrok 或 X Premium+ 订阅）：浏览器里打开 xAI 的确认页，核对手机上显示的短码后同意。这项登录借用 xAI 官方命令行工具的公开登录入口，不是 xAI 专门给 Mika 开的，xAI 可能限制这种用法；有的订阅档位登录后仍不能调用（提示 403），那时改用 xAI 的 API Key。
- **OpenRouter**：OpenRouter 官方给第三方应用的授权。同意后 OpenRouter 给 Mika 一把属于你的 Key（名字是 Mika），用量从你的 OpenRouter 余额里扣；不想用了，在 OpenRouter 的 Keys 页面删掉它。

退出登录只清这台手机上的登录信息。

## 查看当前额度

打开 **设置 › 模型 › Token 用量**。顶部按已配置的服务商显示当前额度，下方可以按日期查看本机记录的历史 Token 用量。

DeepSeek、Kimi 和硅基流动显示账户余额。OpenRouter 显示当前 Key 剩余可支出金额，点该行可在 OpenRouter 查看账户余额。ChatGPT 等服务商可点「管理用量」打开官方页面。点「刷新」可以重新查询当前额度。

## 思考强度

用 ChatGPT 登录、xAI 登录或 Responses 接口的模型，可在各用途卡片下调整「思考强度」；OpenAI 兼容、Anthropic Messages、Gemini 接口的模型，服务商在模型列表里写明了这个模型的档位时也可以调。默认用服务商默认值；选「用主模型」时也跟随它的强度，明确选同一个模型则可分别设置。档位优先采用服务商报告的列表（Anthropic 的模型列表逐个写明支持哪些档位，只能按预算思考的模型没有档位）；没报告时只有 Responses 一类提供手动选项，实际支持情况以服务端为准，OpenAI 兼容、Anthropic、Gemini 不猜。更高强度通常更慢、消耗更多 token。

## 响应速度

打开「设置 → 模型 → 服务商」，点开 OpenAI（API Key）或 ChatGPT 服务商里的具体模型，在「用作」面板里选「响应速度」。默认沿用服务端设置，也可以选 Fast 或 Ultrafast。这个设置随服务商和模型保存，对使用该模型的各个用途生效。加速档位由 OpenAI 按模型、项目或订阅授权，可能增加 API 费用或套餐用量。服务端拒绝某个档位时，可以切回「默认」。

## 上下文窗口与压缩

在「设置 › 模型」的用途卡片下打开「上下文与压缩」。窗口留空时沿用所选模型的窗口，压缩触发点留空时自动计算；也可以分别填入 token 数。触发点按整份请求计，包含系统提示词、工具定义和消息。比如窗口填 1,000,000 时，自动触发点为 967,000，也可以手填 600,000 提前压缩。输入时只写数字。界面显示允许范围和实际生效值，压缩后会留出一段余量再触发。

设置按服务商和模型保存，使用同一模型的各用途共享，下次任务生效。「重置」后保存即可恢复自动。以后重新选择模型导致窗口变小时，实际触发点会限制在新窗口的允许范围内。窗口覆盖只影响本地预算，服务端仍有自己的上下文上限。

## 用自己电脑或局域网里跑的模型

添加服务商时选「自定义」，接口地址填 `http://` 开头的也行，比如 `http://192.168.1.10:11434/v1`（手机和那台电脑在同一个 Wi-Fi 下）。本机和局域网的地址不加提示；不加密又不在局域网里的地址会提醒一句：API Key 和对话内容可能被同一网络里的人看到，能用 `https://` 就用。

## 网络代理

不想开全局 VPN、又需要代理才能连上模型服务时，在「设置 › 网络代理」填一个地址：`http://主机:端口` 或 `socks5://主机:端口`（`socks5h` 也行，域名都交给代理解析），需要账号密码时写成 `http://用户:密码@主机:端口`。地址加密保存在手机上，界面上只显示协议、主机和端口。

- 走这个代理的：调模型（对话、语音转文字、连接测试）、列模型、查询服务商额度、用账号登录时换令牌、在 App 里下载更新、内置浏览器，以及「文件与计算环境」里的命令（那里允许联网时）。
- 始终直连的：这台手机和局域网里的地址（localhost、127.x、10.x、172.16–31.x、192.168.x、100.64–127.x、`.local`、`.lan` 结尾的名字、不带点的机器名），所以 Ollama、LM Studio 这类本地模型不受影响。
- 连不上代理、或代理拒了账号密码时，会直接说是代理的问题，不会说成 Key 或模型不对。
- `https://` 开头的代理（先和代理本身建加密连接）只有「文件与计算环境」里的命令用得上，Mika 自己的连接照旧直连；想全部走代理请用 `http://` 或 `socks5://`。
- 内置浏览器要手机的 WebView 支持单独设代理才会走它；带账号密码的 SOCKS 代理浏览器用不了。这两种情况设置页那一行会写明浏览器直连。

## ChatGPT 换账号后提示工作区无权访问

如果浏览器提示“此应用仅对其工作区成员可用”，诊断代码为 `3p_login_workspace_scope_denied`，先确认选的是原先授权的 ChatGPT 账号及工作区。这个错误表示当前登录不符合该应用注册的工作区范围；不要仅凭它判断密码错误或套餐额度耗尽。

Mika 的 ChatGPT“退出登录”会保留注册的 `client_id`，供同一个账号再次登录。若你确实要换到另一个账号／工作区，反复退出再登录可能仍沿用旧绑定。可以重新建立连接：

1. 回到 Mika，取消仍在等待的登录。
2. 记下当前主模型、看图模型和轻量模型的选择。
3. 打开“设置 › 模型 › ChatGPT”，点底部的“删除这个服务商”并确认。它会删除该服务商的本机凭据、模型配置及注册 ID，正在使用它的用途需要重新选择；聊天记录保留。无需卸载 Mika 或清除整个 App 的数据。
4. 重新添加 ChatGPT 服务商，点“使用 ChatGPT 继续”，在浏览器选择要用的账号及工作区，完成授权后回到 Mika。
5. 重新选择各用途的模型，再发一条简短请求验证。取得模型列表只能证明登录／列模型成功，不能代替实际调用测试。

这条路径用于更换账号／工作区，不是绕过工作区访问控制。若新建连接后仍被拒绝，请确认账号有该工作区的访问权限，或联系工作区管理员；反馈时提供错误代码和 Mika 版本，遮掉邮箱、授权码及令牌。


### Ask and Autonomous

# Ask and Autonomous

[简体中文](modes.md) | English

When Mika works for you, the mode decides which steps it checks with you first. There is one global switch: "Developer options" (开发者选项) → "Autonomous mode" (自主模式) in Settings. Off means Ask, on means Autonomous.

| Mode | Behavior |
|---|---|
| **Ask** (default) | Only the step that spends money is confirmed with you first: placing or submitting an order, or a confirm/submit while the page shows an amount due. The card says where, what and how much, and you can approve just this once or decline. The payment itself is done by you. Sending messages, posting, submitting forms, deleting and changing settings are not asked about; they are just done. |
| **Autonomous** | Does not ask even before paying. The spacing between items in batch jobs still applies. |

- The switch applies to all tasks from then on; if a running task switches from Ask to Autonomous, payments are no longer asked about from the next step.
- In both modes Mika asks you to take over for things only you should do, like logging in, verification codes and payment passwords. It also asks when information is missing or only you can decide (e.g. which of two contacts with the same name).
- For tasks that run while you are away, such as scheduled tasks, Ask mode does not wait at a money-spending step: it skips it and tells you plainly which step was not done. Everything else is completed as usual.

You are responsible for actions you approve, and for actions Mika takes on your behalf in Autonomous mode. For anything important, use Ask mode and check the results; see the [disclaimer](disclaimer.en.md).

### 询问与自主

# 询问与自主

简体中文 | [English](modes.en.md)

Mika 替你办事时，有两种模式决定哪些步骤要先问你。全局一个开关：设置里的「开发者选项」→「自主模式」，关着是询问，打开是自主。

| 模式 | 行为 |
|---|---|
| **询问**（默认） | 只有花钱的那一步先问你：下单、提交订单，或者页面上显示着应付金额时的确认、提交。卡片上写明在哪、买什么、多少钱，只能同意这一次或不同意。付款本身由你亲手完成。发消息、发帖、提交表单、删除、改设置这些都不问，直接做完。 |
| **自主** | 连付款也不先问你，直接做完。成批做事时两次之间的间隔照样保留。 |

- 换了开关管之后的所有任务；正在做的任务从询问换成自主，下一步起付款也不再问。
- 登录、验证码、付款密码这类要你亲手处理的事，两种模式都会请你接管；信息不够、或者只有你能选（比如两个同名联系人选哪个）时，也会问你。
- 定时任务等你不在场的任务，在询问模式下遇到要花钱的一步不会等人，会直接不做，并照实告诉你哪一步没做成；别的照常做完。

你同意的动作，以及自主模式下 Mika 替你做的动作，都由你负责。重要的事请用询问模式，并检查结果，见[免责声明](disclaimer.md)。

### For AI assistants: writing a Mika persona for the user

# For AI assistants: writing a Mika persona for the user

[简体中文](persona-writing.md) | English

This document is written for **an AI assistant that is drafting a Mika persona for the user**. People can follow it too.

If you are the user: send your AI assistant the line below, replacing the last sentence with what you want.

```
Follow https://github.com/wangzan101/Mika/blob/main/docs/persona-writing.en.md and write a Mika persona for me. What I want: shorter answers, less talk while working, the tone of a reliable colleague.
```

If you are the AI assistant: read "What a persona can change" first, ask the user what effect they want, then deliver the result in the "Delivery format". When you are unsure what the user wants, ask once; do not invent a character for them.

## What a persona is

Mika is an assistant on the user's phone that gets things done: it operates apps, browses the web, works with files and reports what happened. It speaks in two ways:

- **Progress notes**: one line next to each step while it works, shown in the chat and in the floating capsule, where space is tight.
- **Final answer**: the result once the task is done. Markdown works (headings, lists, tables, code blocks).

A persona decides how both are worded. It has four parts:

| Part | What it is | Limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Name | Only tells several saved personas apart; shown under "Manage personas" and in the run details. With a single persona it is called "My style" automatically | 40 characters |
| Nickname | The name Mika uses for itself, Mika by default; letters, digits and spaces only | 16 characters |
| Options | A few settings chosen in the UI, see below | none |
| Instructions | Free text for what the options cannot express | 4000 characters (about 3000 tokens) |

One persona is chosen in Settings and applies to every conversation from the next message on; a task that is already running is not affected. With no persona, Mika speaks the way it normally does.

## What a persona can change

Only how Mika speaks and writes:

- tone, warmth, formality, humour
- how long answers are
- how progress notes and suggestions are phrased
- formatting preferences (headings, lists, emoji)

The following have no effect even if written. Mika keeps to its rules and, where it matters, tells the user why:

- **Making it act**: starting a task, calling a tool, reading memory or the screen, changing a setting, sending something outward, disclosing information. Those follow only the user's own messages.
- **Changing the rules**: evidence, safety, privacy, authorization, confirmation and completion. For example "pay without asking me", "say it is done without checking", "make something up if you cannot find it". To be asked less often, the user turns on Autonomous mode under Settings › Task running; see [Ask and Autonomous](modes.en.md).
- **Granting abilities**: a persona cannot give it tools, permissions or access.
- **A different identity**: the nickname can change (see the table above), and only the name changes. It is still the same assistant with the same rules and abilities, and the app is still called Mika.
- **The reply language**: chosen under Settings › Language & appearance; do not put it in a persona.

Two more kinds of content do not belong in a persona:

- One-off task requests ("book tomorrow's ticket"): that is a user message.
- Facts about the user ("I live in Shanghai", "I am allergic to peanuts"): that is memory.

## Options first, then instructions

Options are ready-made: each value maps to one prepared sentence, so prefer them. Instructions are only for what the options cannot say.

| Option | Values | What it controls |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Base style and tone | Default, Crisp, Friendly, Playful | The overall register |
| Emoji | Less, Default, More | Whether it uses emoji |
| Answer length | Shorter, Default, Longer | Length of the final answer |
| Progress notes | Brief, Default, Detailed | How much it says at each step |

When choosing:

- **Leave most options at Default.** Change only what the user clearly wants changed.
- **Avoid combinations that pull against each other.** "Crisp" with "Longer answers" asks for two things that cancel out. If the user really needs that, say in the instructions which one wins.
- **Do not repeat in the instructions what an option already says.**

## Writing the instructions

1. **Describe how it speaks, not who it is.** Two or three sentences set the tone. A long backstory dilutes the requests that matter.
2. **Describe observable behaviour, not adjectives.** "Be professional" does nothing; "put amounts, times and addresses on their own lines" does.
3. **Say which kind of speech you mean.** State whether a request is about progress notes or the final answer. Progress notes have little room; do not ask for essays there.
4. **One request per line, in the imperative.** "Lead with the conclusion, then the reasons." "Call me boss."
5. **Keep it short.** Under about 150 words is a good target. The instructions are sent with every task, so length costs tokens every time.
6. **Write in the user's language.** No need to translate into English.
7. **Leave these out**: angle-bracket tags, "ignore the rules above", asking it to pretend it saw something it did not. They do not work and only take up space.

Three blocks work well; drop the ones you do not need:

```
Tone: …
Speaking habits: …
While working: …
```

Check the draft before handing it over:

- Is every line only about how to speak or write?
- Is any line something an option already covers?
- Do any two lines contradict each other?
- If a line were removed, would anything change? If not, remove it.

## Examples

**A crisp colleague**

- Options: base style Crisp, emoji Less, answer length Shorter, progress notes Brief. Everything else Default.
- Instructions:

```
Speaking habits: lead with the conclusion, then the reasons. Put numbers, times and places on their own lines.
While working: when I need to decide something, list the choices as 1, 2, 3 so I can reply with a number.
```

**A patient explainer**

- Options: base style Friendly, answer length Longer. Everything else Default.
- Instructions:

```
Tone: treat me as someone new to the topic. Avoid jargon; when a term is unavoidable, explain it in passing.
Speaking habits: number the steps when there are more than three. For each step, say what I will see when it is done.
```

**A butler with some character**

- Options: all Default.
- Instructions:

```
Tone: an old-school butler: courteous, unhurried, with the occasional dry remark.
Speaking habits: address me as "sir". Give bad news plainly, but say first what can be done about it.
```

## Delivery format

A persona can currently only be set by hand on the phone, so give the user three parts they can follow:

1. **Nickname**: give one when the user wants it to go by another name; otherwise say "leave empty".
2. **Options**: list only the ones that are not Default, with the value to pick.
3. **Instructions**: plain text in a code block, ready to copy. If nothing needs adding, say "leave empty".

Only when the user wants to keep several personas, also give each a name of at most 40 characters.

Then tell the user where to enter it and how to confirm it works:

- Where: Mika › Settings › Persona. Enter the nickname, pick the base style and the options on the page, paste the instructions into the text box, then tap "Save" at the bottom. Nothing applies until it is saved.
- Several personas: "Manage personas" at the bottom of the page creates, renames, copies and deletes them; tap one and choose "Use this one" and every conversation follows it. "Preview the full prompt" there shows the exact text sent to the model.
- Confirm: send a message; the run details for that turn (expand "More details") show which persona was used.

## Related References

- [异步路由分发机制 Reference](https://blog.ai-hao123.com)
- [RESTful微服务治理 Reference](https://blog.ai-hao123.com/sitemap.xml)
- [中间件管道调用契约 Reference](https://www.ai-hao123.com/d/uz612724.html)


### 给 AI 助手：帮用户写 Mika 人格

# 给 AI 助手：帮用户写 Mika 人格

简体中文 | [English](persona-writing.en.md)

这份文档是写给**帮用户起草 Mika 人格的 AI 助手**看的。人也可以照着写。

如果你是用户：把下面这句话发给你的 AI 助手，后半句换成你想要的效果。

```
请按 https://github.com/wangzan101/Mika/blob/main/docs/persona-writing.md 的要求，帮我写一个 Mika 人格。我想要的效果是：回答短一点，办事时少说话，语气像靠谱的同事。
```

如果你是 AI 助手：先读完「人格能改什么」，向用户问清想要的效果，再按「交付格式」给出结果。拿不准用户要什么时问一次，不要替用户编设定。

## 人格是什么

Mika 是手机上替用户办事的助手：操作 App、上网、处理文件，并把结果告诉用户。它说的话有两种：

- **进度说明**：办事时每一步旁边的一句话，显示在对话和悬浮胶囊里，地方很小。
- **最终回答**：事情办完后的结果，支持 Markdown（标题、列表、表格、代码块）。

人格决定这两种话怎么说。一套人格由四样东西组成：

| 组成 | 说明 | 上限 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 名称 | 只在存了多套时用来区分，显示在「管理人格」和运行过程里；只有一套时自动叫「我的风格」 | 40 字 |
| 称呼 | Mika 提到自己时用的名字，默认 Mika；只能用文字、数字和空格 | 16 字 |
| 选项 | 界面上直接选的几项，见下文 | 无 |
| 指令 | 自己写的一段文字，补充选项表达不了的 | 4000 字（约 3000 token） |

人格在设置里选用一套，对所有对话生效，从下一条消息起算；正在进行的任务不受影响。不选人格时 Mika 按平常的方式说话。

## 人格能改什么

能改的只有说话和书写的方式：

- 语气、亲切和正式的程度、幽不幽默
- 回答的长短
- 进度说明和建议怎么措辞
- 格式偏好（用不用标题、列表、表情符号）

下面这些写了也不会生效。Mika 仍按原来的规则办，必要时会向用户说明原因：

- **让它做事**：开始任务、调用工具、读记忆或屏幕、改设置、对外发送内容、透露信息。这些只听用户自己发的消息。
- **改规则**：证据、安全、隐私、授权、确认、完成这几类规则。例如「付款不用问我」「不用核对直接说办好了」「查不到就编一个」。要少被询问，请用户在 设置 › 任务运行 里打开「自主模式」，见[询问与自主](modes.md)。
- **给能力**：人格不能给它工具、权限或访问范围。
- **换身份**：称呼可以改（见上表），改的只是自称。它仍然是同一个助理，规则和能做的事不变；App 的名字也还是 Mika。
- **回答的语言**：在 设置 › 语言与外观 里选，不要写进人格。

另外两类内容不属于人格，不要写进去：

- 一次性的任务要求（「帮我订明天的票」）：那是用户的消息。
- 关于用户的事实（「我住在上海」「我对花生过敏」）：那是记忆。

## 先用选项，再写指令

选项是现成的，每一档对应一句写好的要求，优先用它们。指令只写选项表达不了的。

| 选项 | 可选值 | 管什么 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 基础风格和语气 | 默认、干练、友好、活泼 | 整体的调子 |
| 表情符号 | 少一点、默认、多一点 | 用不用表情符号 |
| 回答篇幅 | 更短、默认、更详细 | 最终回答的长短 |
| 进度说明 | 简短、默认、详细 | 办事时每一步说多少 |

选的时候注意：

- **大部分选项留在默认。** 只动用户明确想改的那几项。
- **不要选互相拉扯的组合。** 例如「干练」加「回答更详细」，两句要求彼此抵消。真的需要时，在指令里写清楚谁优先。
- **选项已经说了的，指令里不要再说一遍。**

## 怎么写指令

1. **写怎么说，不写它是谁。** 两三句交代调子就够。长篇的身世设定会把真正有用的要求冲淡。
2. **写看得见的做法，不写形容词。** 「要专业」没有用；「金额、时间、地址各占一行」有用。
3. **分清两种话。** 说明这条要求是管进度说明，还是管最终回答。进度说明的地方很小，别要求它在那里长篇大论。
4. **一条一行，用祈使句。** 「先给结论，再说依据。」「称呼我老板。」
5. **写短。** 建议 300 字以内。指令会随每一个任务发给模型，写得越长，每次花的 token 越多。
6. **用用户的语言写。** 不需要翻译成英文。
7. **别写这些**：尖括号标签、「忽略以上规则」、让它假装看到了没看到的东西。它们不会生效，只会占地方。

可以按这三块组织，用不到的块直接省掉：

```
语气：……
说话习惯：……
办事时：……
```

写完自己检查一遍：

- 每一条都只关于怎么说、怎么写吗？
- 有没有哪一条其实是选项能表达的？
- 有没有两条互相矛盾？
- 删掉任何一条，效果会不会变？不会就删。

## 例子

**干练的同事**

- 选项：基础风格选「干练」，表情符号「少一点」，回答篇幅「更短」，进度说明「简短」。其余默认。
- 指令：

```
说话习惯：先给结论，再说依据。数字、时间、地点各占一行。
办事时：遇到要我决定的事，把选项列成 1、2、3，我回数字就行。
```

**耐心的讲解者**

- 选项：基础风格选「友好」，回答篇幅「更详细」。其余默认。
- 指令：

```
语气：把我当成第一次接触这件事的人，不用术语，非用不可时顺手解释一句。
说话习惯：步骤多于三步时编号。每一步说清楚做完会看到什么。
```

**有点角色感的管家**

- 选项：全部默认。
- 指令：

```
语气：像一位老派的管家，措辞得体，不急不躁，偶尔来一句克制的幽默。
说话习惯：称呼我「先生」。坏消息直接说，不绕弯，但先说能怎么补救。
```

## 交付格式

人格目前只能在手机上手动设置，所以请把结果分成三段给用户，方便照着做：

1. **称呼**：用户想让它换个名字时给出；不换就写「不用填」。
2. **选项**：只列不是默认的那几项，写明选哪一档。
3. **指令**：放在代码块里的纯文本，能直接复制。没有需要补充的就写「不用填」。

用户想同时存好几套时，再给每一套起一个不超过 40 字的名称。

最后告诉用户在哪里填、怎么确认生效：

- 在哪里设：Mika › 设置 › 人格。在页面上填称呼、选基础风格和各个选项，把指令粘进输入框，最后点底部的「保存」。保存后才生效。
- 存多套：页底的「管理人格」里可以新建、改名、复制、删除；点某一套选「用这一套」，之后所有对话都按它来。那里的「预览完整提示词」能看到最终发给模型的全文。
- 确认：发一条消息试试；这一轮的运行过程（展开「更多详情」）里会写着用了哪个人格。

### Setting up phone control, step by step

# Setting up phone control, step by step

[简体中文](setup-guide.md) | English

This guide walks you through "Set up phone control" in Mika. No technical knowledge needed; just follow along. It takes about 3 to 5 minutes.

## Before you start

- **What you need**: an Android phone running Android 12 or later (Mika installs on Android 11 but can't use apps there; Android 14 or later recommended), connected to any Wi-Fi network (internet access not required, just being connected is enough).
- **Why this is needed**: Mika uses apps for you on an invisible "background screen", so you can keep using your own screen. To do that, Mika borrows Android's built-in "Wireless debugging" to start a small built-in helper.
- **Everything happens on the phone**: no computer, no cable.
- **You do it once**: after pairing once, Mika connects by itself. Even if the system later turns wireless debugging off, Mika turns it back on, with your permission.
- **Optional**: web, files and chat work without it. You only need it for tasks that use apps on your phone.

> The paths below follow stock Android. Some phones name or place menus differently. If you can't find something, use the search box at the top of system Settings (search for "Build number", "Developer options" or "Wireless debugging").

## Where to find the wizard

- The first time you open Mika, "Set up phone control" is the last step after setting up a model.
- If you tapped "Not now" back then, that's fine: open Mika's Settings and tap the notice in the status card at the top, or go to Settings › Phone control › Pair again.
- If a task needs your phone before you've set it up, a line appears in the chat; tap "Open Settings".

The wizard is a numbered checklist of six steps. **Each step ticks itself off when it's done**: Mika checks the system switches by itself, so you usually don't need to press "Next". The current step is highlighted and has a button that takes you straight to the right system settings page; when you're done there, press Back to return to Mika.

Some phones can't report these switches, or report them wrong: you've turned a setting on but Mika stays on that step. Then tap "I’ve turned it on, next" under the step to carry on; the wizard never locks you in. What counts in the end is pairing and connecting: once Mika connects, setup is done. You can also tap any ticked step to go back and redo it.

<!-- Screenshot: the six-step checklist in "Set up phone control" -->

---

## Step 1: Turn on Developer options

**In Mika**: tap "Open About phone".

**In system settings**:

1. Go to Settings › About phone.
2. Scroll all the way down to "Build number".
3. **Tap "Build number" 7 times quickly in a row.** Along the way you'll see "You are now X steps away from being a developer". If your phone has a screen lock, you'll be asked for your PIN or password once.
4. When you see "You are now a developer!" (or similar), you're done.

<!-- Screenshot: "Build number" on the About phone page -->

**How to tell it worked**: back in Mika, step 1 shows "On" with a tick.

**Common snags**:

- Can't find "Build number": on some phones it's inside "Software information" or "Version" under "About phone". You can also search Settings for "Build number".
- Nothing happens: tap in quick succession without long pauses.
- "No need, you are already a developer": it was already on; just go back to Mika.
- It's on but Mika stays on this step: tap "I’ve turned it on, next" to continue.

## Step 2: Turn on USB debugging

> Note: in Developer options, don't change any switch this guide doesn't mention. Setup only needs "USB debugging" here and "Wireless debugging" in step 4. Some switches can erase the phone: "Boot with 16 KB page size", for example, asks to erase all data on some phones. If you see a prompt to erase data, reformat or factory reset the phone, tap "Cancel", not "Erase all data".

**In Mika**: tap "Open Developer options".

**In system settings**:

1. Go to Settings › System › Developer options (Mika takes you there).
2. Scroll to "USB debugging" and turn it on.
3. When asked "Allow USB debugging?", tap "OK".

<!-- Screenshot: the "USB debugging" switch in Developer options -->

**No cable needed.** With it on, Mika can keep working even when Wi-Fi is off, once pairing is done.

**How to tell it worked**: back in Mika, step 2 is ticked.

**Common snags**:

- Can't find "Developer options": on stock Android it's under Settings › System; some phones put it under "Additional settings" or similar. Searching Settings for "Developer options" is fastest.
- **Keep USB debugging on** from now on. Turning it off stops phone control.
- It's on but Mika stays on this step: tap "I’ve turned it on, next" to continue.

## Step 3: Turn on Mika's accessibility (we suggest skipping this)

**Suggestion: just tap "Skip (Mika turns it on after pairing)"**, the top button on this step.

Why we suggest skipping:

- Once pairing is done, Mika turns on its own accessibility service **by itself** ("Turn on accessibility for me" in Settings › Recovery & repair is on by default). You don't have to hunt for it in system settings.
- Doing it by hand can get stuck: if Mika wasn't installed from an app store (for example, you downloaded the APK from a web page), Android marks accessibility as a "Restricted setting" and won't let you turn it on directly. When Mika turns it on after pairing, this restriction doesn't get in the way.

The only cost of skipping: in the next steps you type the 6-digit pairing code yourself once (it's easy, see step 5).

<!-- Screenshot: the "Skip (Mika turns it on after pairing)" button on the accessibility step -->

**If accessibility is already on**: this step ticks itself off and Mika reads the pairing code by itself, which is even easier.

**If you really want to turn it on by hand now**: tap "Open Accessibility settings", find Mika in the list, turn it on and confirm. If the switch is greyed out or you see "Restricted setting":

1. Go back to Mika and tap "Can't turn it on? Allow restricted settings in App info first" (or go to Settings › Apps › Mika yourself).
2. On the "App info" page, tap ⋮ (three dots) at the top right and choose "Allow restricted settings", then confirm.
3. Go back to Accessibility settings and turn Mika on.

<!-- Screenshot: "Allow restricted settings" in the ⋮ menu on App info -->

> Note: "Allow restricted settings" only appears in the ⋮ menu **after you've tried once** to turn on accessibility and the system blocked it.

If the system says "An app is obscuring a permission request" when you turn it on: close other apps' floating windows or bubbles (chat bubbles, floating buttons), then try again.

## Step 4: Turn on Wireless debugging

**First make sure the phone is on Wi-Fi** (internet access not required).

**In Mika**: tap "Open Developer options".

**In system settings**:

1. In Developer options, scroll to "Wireless debugging" and turn on the **switch** on its right.
2. When the system asks "Allow wireless debugging on this network?": **tick "Always allow on this network"**, then tap "Allow". With that ticked, Mika can turn wireless debugging on by itself on this Wi-Fi in future.

<!-- Screenshot: "Wireless debugging" in Developer options -->
<!-- Screenshot: the "Allow wireless debugging" dialog with the "Always allow on this network" checkbox -->

**How to tell it worked**: back in Mika, step 4 is ticked.

**Common snags**:

- The switch turns itself off again: usually the phone isn't on Wi-Fi, or "Allow" wasn't tapped in the dialog. Join Wi-Fi and try again.
- The switch is on but Mika stays on this step: some phones don't report this switch. Tap "I’ve turned it on, next" to continue.
- There's no "Wireless debugging" in Developer options at all: tap "Can’t find Wireless debugging?" in this step and start it from a computer instead (see [Another way](#another-way-start-it-from-a-computer-usb-cable) below).

## Step 5: Pair with a code

**The one thing that trips people up**: the pairing code only works while the system's pairing dialog is open. **As soon as the dialog closes (switching apps, pressing Back, locking the screen), the code is no longer valid.** So stay on the pairing dialog while you enter the code; don't switch apps.

**Before you start**: at this step Mika asks for permission to send notifications. Please tap "Allow": without accessibility, the pairing code is entered in Mika's notification. If notifications are off, the main button on this step is to turn them on first:

- Mika isn't allowed to send notifications: the wizard says "The pairing code goes into a notification, so allow Mika’s notifications first." Tap "Allow notifications".
- Allowed, but Mika's "Pairing" notifications are turned off: tap "Turn on “Pairing” notifications" and turn them on in the system notification settings.
- "Pairing" notifications are set not to pop up: the wizard mentions it; tap "Turn on" and turn on "Pop on screen". You can also skip that and enter the code from the notification shade.

**In Mika**: tap "Open Wireless debugging".

**In system settings**:

1. Mika takes you to Developer options with the "Wireless debugging" row highlighted. **Tap the words "Wireless debugging"** (not the switch) to open its page.
2. Tap "Pair device with pairing code".
3. A dialog appears with a **6-digit pairing code** and an "IP address & port".

<!-- Screenshot: "Pair device with pairing code" on the Wireless debugging page -->
<!-- Screenshot: the pairing dialog showing the 6-digit code -->

Then one of two things happens:

### Case A: accessibility is already on — nothing to do

The wizard shows a green hint: "When the code appears, wait a few seconds — Mika reads it and finishes pairing." Stay on the pairing dialog and **wait a few seconds**. Mika reads the code and pairs by itself, and the dialog closes on its own.

Some phones pause Mika's accessibility as soon as you open system Settings, and then Mika can't read the code. If nothing happens after a few seconds, **swipe down from the top of the screen** and type the 6 digits into Mika's "Enter pairing code" notification in the shade (same as in case B below). The pairing dialog stays open.

### Case B: accessibility is off (you skipped step 3) — enter the code in the notification

The wizard shows this as three small steps: ① Tap “Pair device with pairing code” ② Mika’s notification pops up at the top of the screen; if not, swipe down to open the notification shade ③ Tap “Enter code” and type the 6 digits. In detail:

1. **Don't leave the pairing dialog.** Note the 6 digits.
2. As soon as the pairing dialog opens, Mika's notification "Enter pairing code" pops up at the top of the screen, saying "Type the 6 digits shown on screen here — no need to leave the pairing window". If nobody answers it, it pops up again a little later, at most three more times.
   - If it doesn't pop up, or disappears quickly: **swipe down from the top of the screen** to open the notification shade, and you'll find it there. Pulling down the shade doesn't close the pairing dialog.
3. Tap "Enter code" on the notification. An input box labelled "6 digits" appears.
4. Type the 6 digits and tap send (the arrow next to the box). Spaces, dashes or full-width digits are fine.
5. The notification changes to "Pairing…", then a few seconds later to "Paired", and goes away by itself.

<!-- Screenshot: Mika's "Enter pairing code" notification with the input box in the notification shade -->

**Tips**:

- Allow Mika's notifications first. If you haven't, the wizard shows a note and an "Allow notifications" button.
- If the wizard shows an orange note saying "Needs you" and "Task results" notifications won't pop up: that's about notifications during later tasks, not pairing. You can tap "Turn on", or ignore it for now.
- If what you typed isn't 6 digits, the notification says "Enter 6 digits, then try again" right away and keeps the input box; nothing is sent.
- If the code was wrong or expired, the notification says "Wrong or expired code: in the pairing window, tap “Pair device with pairing code” again to get a new code, then enter it again" and keeps the input box. The same goes if the pairing dialog has already closed: go back to "Wireless debugging" and tap "Pair device with pairing code" again to get a **new** code, then enter the new one.
- Still no notification? The wizard has "No notification? Enter it here". But going back to Mika closes the pairing dialog, so use **split screen**: the pairing dialog on one side, Mika on the other. If Mika hasn't found the pairing dialog yet, it asks for one more number: the digits after the colon in "IP address & port" in the pairing dialog.

**How to tell it worked**: back in Mika, step 5 shows "Paired".

This step has no "Next": pairing has to actually happen. If neither the notification nor reading the code works, use "No notification? Enter it here" described above.

## Step 6: Connect automatically

Nothing to do here. Once paired, Mika connects and gets ready by itself, usually in a few seconds. When you see "Phone control is set up", you're done.

<!-- Screenshot: the wizard showing "Phone control is set up" -->

If you skipped step 3, Mika now turns on its own accessibility service. You can see Mika switched on in the system's Accessibility settings.

To find the Wireless debugging port, Mika first tries the one it used last time, the one the system reports and the one announced on the local network. If none of these works (some routers block those announcements), it searches this phone itself; the wizard shows "Looking for the Wireless debugging port on this phone…" for up to about ten seconds. It only looks at this phone, never at other devices on the same Wi-Fi.

If it still can't find it, the "Connect automatically" step shows "Enter the Wireless debugging port": open the system's "Wireless debugging" page, look at the "IP address & port" line, enter **the number after the colon** (for example `41235` in `192.168.1.5:41235`) and tap "Connect". Mika remembers it once connected. The number changes when you turn Wireless debugging off and on; Mika can usually find the new one by itself, otherwise just enter it again.

While connecting and after a failed connection, "Not now" is always at the bottom, so you can leave at any time and continue later from Settings.

If pairing or connecting fails, Mika uses what it could read to say which earlier step is the most likely cause (for example "“Wireless debugging” seems to be off" or "This phone doesn’t let Mika read the “Wireless debugging” switch"), with a button such as "Back to “Turn on Wireless debugging”" that takes you back to redo that step.

## Another way: start it from a computer (USB cable)

If wireless pairing doesn't work (some vendor ROMs have no working "Wireless debugging" at all), or you'd like an AI agent on your computer to set things up, you can start the same built-in helper from a computer with adb over a USB cable. Both wireless pairing and USB startup provide the adb shell identity that the helper needs. USB debugging already provides that identity, so if the system has removed the "Wireless debugging" entry, there is no need to keep looking for a pairing page or code.

1. Open Mika on the phone once (Mika prepares the start file).
2. Do steps 1 and 2 (Developer options, USB debugging) and connect the phone to the computer with a cable; when the phone asks whether to allow USB debugging, tap "Allow". Confirm system security prompts yourself; do not let a tool simulate the taps.
3. On the computer, run (if more than one device is connected, use `adb -s <serial> shell ...` instead):

```
adb shell sh /sdcard/Android/data/com.wangzan101.mika/files/usb-start.sh
```

When you see `Mika helper starting...`, go back to Mika and check that "Phone control" shows ready. What matters is that the command runs as adb's shell user, not that it comes from a computer: if the phone already has another channel that runs adb shell commands, running the same script through it works too. On most phones you can unplug the cable afterwards and keep using phone control. Some systems stop the helper when the cable is unplugged; if that happens, plug the cable back in and run this command once more to restore it. The wizard doesn't show this option all the time. The same command, with a "Copy" button, appears in the current step as "Can’t use Wireless debugging on this phone? Start from a computer instead" when it's needed: the phone has no Wireless debugging, you tapped "Can’t find Wireless debugging?" in step 4, pairing or connecting failed, or the wizard has been waiting on step 4, step 5 (before the pairing window is found) or "Connect automatically" for about 45 seconds.

Good to know:

- **Run it again after a phone restart.** A helper started this way is gone after a restart and doesn't come back by itself. Without wireless pairing Mika can't start it either, so it shows "Phone helper stopped", and "Set up phone control" shows this command with a "Copy" button instead of sending you to look for Wireless debugging. After a restart, open Mika once (it prepares a fresh start file), then run the same command.
- If the phone has a working "Wireless debugging", pairing once (steps 4 and 5) lets Mika reconnect by itself after restarts, with no computer. Phones without it need the command after every restart.
- After starting this way, steps 4 and 5 show as "Skipped" in the wizard, and Mika doesn't ask you to turn on Wireless debugging while the helper is connected.
- If it says `Mika helper did not start` or `is not running`, open Mika once, then run the same command again.
- After a Mika update, also open Mika once before running it.
- The start file holds a one-time code only while the helper isn't connected, and the code stops working once used; while the helper is connected, the file only says it's already running.

## Rooted phone: start it with root

If your phone is rooted (Mika can find `su`), you can start the same built-in helper with root, with no pairing and no computer. Mika shows the Root entry under Settings › Advanced & other only when it detects `su`:

1. Go to Settings › Advanced & other › Root and tap the “Start the phone helper with root” row to explicitly allow Mika to use root.
2. When the system asks for root permission, allow Mika.
3. Check that “Phone control” shows ready. Once authorized, root startup has no switch and is preferred automatically.

Good to know:

- **It comes back by itself after a restart.** When the phone restarts or the helper stops, Mika starts it again with root, without pairing or a computer.
- **The helper's permissions don't change.** A helper started with root still runs as the same limited user as one started over Wireless debugging or from a computer, so Mika can do exactly the same things.
- **Opening the app doesn't suddenly request permission.** You must approve the first request yourself. If root is denied or nobody answers, Mika doesn't keep asking; Root settings explain what happened and tapping the row asks once more.
- **Revoked or unavailable root falls back.** Mika still uses existing Wireless debugging pairing or USB startup where available; otherwise Root settings explain that you need to authorize again or choose another startup method.
- Some root managers hide `su` from apps by default. If you don't see this entry, allow Mika in your root manager first.
- **Root commands (optional, off by default).** The same page has “Allow Mika to run root commands”. After you turn it on and confirm the risk, Mika can run commands as root when something you ask for really needs it (such as reading another app's data or tidying system files). Root commands can change or delete anything on the phone: in Ask mode, every command that changes or deletes something first shows you the full command on a confirmation card and runs only if you approve; read-only commands (listing folders, viewing files, querying a database) run directly. Leave it off if you don't need it.

---

## After setup

- **Keep USB debugging on.** Turning it off stops phone control.
- **The system may turn wireless debugging off**: Android turns it off when Wi-Fi disconnects or changes, and after a restart. That's normal. Mika doesn't need it day to day, only when restarting its built-in helper (for example after a phone restart or a Mika update). "Turn on Wireless debugging automatically" and "Restore after restart" in Settings › Recovery & repair are on by default, so Mika turns it back on for you while on Wi-Fi, with no new pairing code.
- **The first time on a new Wi-Fi network**: the system hasn't allowed wireless debugging on that network yet, so Mika can't turn it on. Turn on "Wireless debugging" once yourself and, in the dialog, **tick "Always allow on this network"** and tap "Allow". After that, nothing more to do on that Wi-Fi.
- **To start over**: Settings › Phone control › Pair again.
- **To stop using it**: Settings › Phone control › Unpair. You can also remove Mika under Wireless debugging › Paired devices in system settings.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | What to do |
|---|---|
| Can't find "Developer options" | Do step 1 first (tap "Build number" 7 times in "About phone"). Once on, stock Android has it under Settings › System › Developer options; other phones may put it under "Additional settings" or similar. Search Settings for "Developer options". |
| Can't find "Build number" | Scroll down in "About phone"; on some phones it's inside "Software information" or "Version". Or search Settings for "Build number". |
| The Wireless debugging switch turns itself off | Make sure you're on Wi-Fi; in the dialog that appears when you turn it on, tap "Allow" and tick "Always allow on this network". After changing Wi-Fi, allow it once more on the new network. |
| No pairing notification from Mika | Check that Mika is allowed to send notifications and that "Pairing" notifications aren't turned off (the wizard reminds you and gives a button); swipe down from the top to open the notification shade; if it's still not there, use "No notification? Enter it here" in the wizard together with split screen. |
| The pairing notification only shows in the shade and doesn't pop up | "Pairing" notifications are set not to pop up. Tap "Turn on" in the wizard and turn on "Pop on screen" in system settings; or just swipe down to the shade to enter the code. |
| "Wrong or expired pairing code" | The code changes each time the pairing dialog opens. Go back to "Wireless debugging", tap "Pair device with pairing code" again and enter the new 6 digits. |
| "The pairing window closed" | Keep the pairing dialog open while entering the code: don't switch apps, press Back or lock the screen. Open the dialog again and enter the code. |
| Pairing worked, but "Connect automatically" fails | Make sure "Wireless debugging" is still on and the phone is on Wi-Fi, then tap "Retry". If that doesn't help, tap "Pair again". If the wizard points at an earlier step, tap "Back to “…”" to redo it. |
| Stuck at "Connect automatically" / can't find the Wireless debugging port | Turn "Wireless debugging" off and on, then tap "Retry"; switch to a phone hotspot or your home Wi-Fi (some routers stop devices from discovering each other); or in "Enter the Wireless debugging port", enter the number after the colon in "IP address & port" on the "Wireless debugging" page and tap "Connect". |
| A switch is on but the wizard stays on that step | Some phones report switches wrong. Tap "I’ve turned it on, next" to continue; what counts in the end is pairing and connecting. |
| "Wireless debugging isn't allowed on this Wi-Fi yet" | Turn on "Wireless debugging" once yourself; in the dialog, tick "Always allow on this network" and tap "Allow". |
| "Not connected to Wi-Fi" | Join any Wi-Fi network (internet access not required); Mika resumes by itself. |
| "Pairing expired" | Pair again. Turn on "Disable adb authorization timeout" in Developer options so it won't expire again. |
| "Phone helper stopped" | The helper was started with the USB start command and doesn't come back by itself after a phone restart. Open Mika once, then run `adb shell sh /sdcard/Android/data/com.wangzan101.mika/files/usb-start.sh` again (you can copy it in "Set up phone control"). If the phone has a working "Wireless debugging", you can also pair once so it comes back by itself after restarts. |
| "Root access was denied" or "Root didn't answer" | Go to Settings › Advanced & other › Root, tap the “Start the phone helper with root” row to request permission again, and allow Mika in the system prompt. If root startup is unavailable, existing Wireless debugging pairing continues to work. |
| "Root is no longer available" | Mika can't find `su` anymore. Pair Wireless debugging or start from a computer instead; if already paired, Mika falls back to Wireless debugging automatically. |
| Mika's accessibility switch is greyed out / "Restricted setting" | Recommended: skip that step; Mika turns it on after pairing. To do it by hand: try turning it on once so the system blocks it, then go to Settings › Apps › Mika, tap ⋮ at the top right › Allow restricted settings, and go back to Accessibility settings to turn Mika on. |
| Accessibility still off after pairing | Check that "Turn on accessibility for me" in Settings › Recovery & repair is on, and wait a few seconds; if it's still off, turn it on by hand as in the row above. |
| "An app is obscuring a permission request" when turning on accessibility | Close other apps' floating windows or bubbles (chat bubbles, floating buttons), then go back to Accessibility settings and turn Mika on. |
| Stuck and nothing above fits | Tap "Copy diagnostics" at the bottom of the wizard (also inside the failed step, and under About Mika › Send feedback). Look it over, then tap "Copy" or "Share" and send it to the author (WeChat or a GitHub issue). It has the version, phone model, the state of each step and the last error — no API keys, chat content or screen content. |

## Set up but not working well: run the compatibility self-check

Pairing and connecting worked, but tasks can't open apps, taps don't land, or things freeze after a while? Open Settings › Recovery & repair › **Compatibility self-check** and tap "Start". In about 1 minute Mika opens its own test page and system Settings (look only, no taps) on its own virtual display, tries reading the screen, tapping, typing, scrolling and going back, then checks the built-in browser and the sandbox. It doesn't touch your other apps, doesn't change settings and doesn't use the network. Please stay on that page while it runs.

Each check shows pass, partial, failed or skipped, and the ones that didn't pass say why and what to do next. When it finishes, tap "Report on GitHub": the report is copied and the "Device compatibility report" issue page opens; paste the report into "Self-check report" and submit. The report only has the phone model, system version and the result of each check, with no accounts, app lists or your content. You can read it before posting.

- [异步路由分发机制 Reference](https://tech.ai-hao123.com/sitemap.xml)
